convention: mu indexed by NUMBER OF TERMS (Mercer/Goddard), not degree
statement: Both computer-aided components of Mercer's sketch that mu(5) <= 1 + pi/6 (INTEGERS 19 (2019) #A20, Section 6 pp. 19-20) now hold by exact arithmetic. (ii) His Table 6 — "a finite search (aided by computer)" for the eligible (r,s,u,v) among fractions in (0,1) with denominator < 6 under r+s=t, u+v=w, r<u, s<v, r(1+v)=u(1+s) with t,w denominator-bounded — was re-run in exact rational arithmetic over the full finite domain: exactly his six printed quadruples survive, no seventh. (iii) His Table 7 case checks — for each derived primitive 4-tuple (a,b,c,d), |1+z^a+z^b+z^c+z^d| <= 1+pi/6 at SOME |z|=1 — are certified by one exact evaluation each at z = -1: every tuple has two or three odd exponents, so |f(-1)|^2 = 1 exactly, and 1 <= (1+piLo/6)^2 with piLo a dyadic rational strictly below pi (certified enclosure), giving min|f| <= 1 <= 1+piLo/6 < 1+pi/6 with no rounding anywhere. What this record does NOT certify: component (i), Mercer's prose assembly for m=6 — see sketchAnatomy.

sketchAnatomy.mIndependentSteps: proven in his completed pi/5 section (pp. 13-18) with derivations that never reference the denominator bound: the six gcd equations rd=b-a, sd=c-b, td=c-a, uc=b-a, vc=d-b, wc=d-a; the constraints r+s=t, u+v=w, u>r, v>s, r(1+v)=u(1+s); and the at-most-one-primitive-multiple lemma (row reduction, p. 17). He states the m-generalization explicitly on p. 16: "this remains true if we change our goal ... to showing mu(5) <= 1+pi/m ... fractions between 0 and 1 whose denominators are less than m".

computerAidedComponents.table6Search: CERTIFIED — re-derived in exact rational arithmetic over the complete finite domain; set-equal to his printed table, both directions
computerAidedComponents.table7CaseChecks: CERTIFIED — six exact point evaluations, each landing at z = -1 with |f(-1)|^2 = 1 exactly, compared exactly against (1+piLo/6)^2

sketchAnatomy.remaining: component (i) is prose Mercer explicitly labels an outline ("We will give a rough outline", p. 19); a certificate cannot rule prose. The honest sentence is: mu(5) <= 1 + pi/6 holds with every computer-aided step of Mercer's outline certified exact — not "theorem, unconditionally". Whether the outline's assembly is complete is a mathematical judgment for a referee, and the m-independent steps it leans on are proven in his own pi/5 section.
